articles.title: “A LITTLE REVIVING”
articles.author: A. B. Parker
articles.place: Substance of word in meeting for ministry, Plainfield, N.J.

paragraphs.text: The brethren will know that these verses occur in a chapter in which Ezra refers to himself as being overwhelmed—“I sat overwhelmed until the evening oblation” (Ezra 9: 4). Having arrived at Jerusalem he found that many of the people had been unfaithful and had taken wives of the nations, having disobeyed Jehovah’s commandment that they should maintain separation from the people of the land.

We do well to cultivate the acquaintance of Ezra, getting to know something of his depth of feeling. He was a very priestly man raised up of Jehovah. He would be such as Zechariah refers to (Zechariah 3: 7, 8) “these that stand by” and “men of portent”. Indeed, the king of Persia refers to him as “an accomplished scribe of the law of God”, Ezra 7: 12. He wrote the books of Chronicles, as far as we know, and as we read those books, comparing them with the books of Samuel and the Kings, we can see, from touches he gives, that he had gained spiritually through being with God in circumstances of discipline and governmental pressure.

This chapter also lets us into his depth of exercise. It contains the remarkable expression that Jehovah had given His people “a little reviving”. Years ago Mr. Taylor asked the brethren to take note of that scripture as bearing on the present day.
We need to be preserved, dear brethren, from

being high-minded. When Ezra wrote 2 Chronicles, he told, in detail, how Rehoboam, after Jehovah had divided Israel because of Solomon’s breakdown, strengthened his kingdom (Judah and Benjamin) and God helped him. But when he became strong he turned aside from the commandments of Jehovah. Jehovah was angry and was minded to deliver up Judah, but He sent Shemaiah, the prophet, to Rehoboam, and he and the rulers humbled themselves. God graciously spared them, saying, “I will grant them a little deliverance”, 2 Chronicles 2: 7.

When we consider that Judah represents the remnant that is recovered from Babylon later, we can see how frail is the line of fidelity. The ten tribes, carried away beyond Babylon will not be recovered until the millennial day. Judah and Benjamin are seen as in the recovery to preserve a lamp for David’s sake, and Ezra was in the light of this when he wrote the book of Ezra and said that Jehovah had ‘given us a little reviving’.

We speak of 2 Timothy 2 as our charter in the day of breakdown. If we connect it with what we have been saying it will help us to realise that a remnant is being preserved for Christ’s sake. He sits a Man at the right hand of God, with the feelings of a Man, and in consideration for Him God will preserve a remnant, that He may have companions. He shall be, and is, anointed with oil of gladness above His companions (Hebrews 1: 9). In view of all this let us keep humble, that we may be preserved through the problems and difficulties of the testimony.

The writer to the Hebrews tells us that the beasts whose blood was taken into the holiest were burned without the camp, “Wherefore also Jesus, that he might sanctify the people by his own blood, suffered without the gate—therefore let us go

forth to him without the camp, bearing his reproach”, Hebrews 13: 11, 12. But in that section it is asserted that “we have an altar”. It is good to take account of what we have, dear brethren. We must go on in humility. There will be no recovery of the candlestick publicly.

There was no ark when the people were recovered from Babylon. God is not re-establishing His seat of public government in the assembly. That has been transferred to the four great monarchies of the nations. Not that there is not government in the assembly, but it is not the seat of public government. You may well ask, What do we have? Well, primarily, we can experience what Jesus said, that “where two or three are gathered together unto my name, there am I in the midst of them”, Matthew.18: 20. We can claim the Lord’s presence as we gather to His name, but we cannot claim any public position. It is the day of “a little reviving”.
Ezra refers to things which we have. He was greatly concerned lest they be lost to the people in his day and we should be concerned, equally, as to the present moment. But Ezra says,

“Now for a little space there hath been favour from Jehovah our God, to leave us a remnant to escape”. Thank God, there is a remnant! There are those with whom we can walk. In our spirits we would link on with the work of God wherever it is, because the approach to the service of God, as set out in Ephesians, relates to our being fully able to apprehend with all the saints “what is the breadth and length and depth and height; and to know the love of the Christ which surpasses knowledge”, Ephesians 3: 18. The Spirit of God would help us to embrace, in our spirits, the great principle of the one body. After the recovery from Babylon the people did not offer two goats for a sin offering, as applied to Judah and Benjamin only, but “a sin-offering

offering for all Israel, twelve he-goats, according to the number of the tribes of Israel”, Ezra 6: 17. They were, in principle, bearing the iniquity of the sanctuary for all Israel. And so should we, even though the number with whom we can walk is small.

Not only is there a remnant with whom we can walk, but, as Ezra said, “… and to give us a nail in his holy place”. Do we value that? His holy place is the sanctuary. It is the place where the pure table and the shewbread are, where the candlestick is, where the golden altar is. We have all that, dear brethren, but only Ezra tells us that we have a nail in His holy place. Much can be said about the holy place—about the typical meaning of the furnishings, the shewbread representing the saints as supported by Christ, according to divine purpose in the presence of God; the candlestick representing Christ as the source of light in that holy environment, so that we need not walk in darkness, but in the light, as God is in it, and can have fellowship with one another; we can spread our matters before God and get the divine answers to all our problems. Then there is the golden altar, signifying our approach to God in prayer. But Ezra tells us there is a nail there. What a comfort! for there are many matters for which we pray that God may not be prepared to answer immediately, and faith would hang such matters on that nail until it is His time to answer them. In Revelation the prayers of saints are said to be preserved in golden bowls, for many of them were uttered in a previous dispensation, but the day is fast approaching when God will have His angels take down those bowls, so to speak, and the prayers will be answered. And He will answer our prayers, too, if in faith we have hung them on the nail in His holy place. They will be answered according to His
will.
Then we have Ezra’s word that God had extended mercy to Judah before the kings of Persia.

Think of the way God has been favourable to us through government. The government of this land is especially favourable to the saints, protecting them and making way for the outgoing of the glad tidings. There are lands where this is not so, but we can give thanks to God that we have favour “before the kings of Persia”, so to speak.

Then he says, “to set up the house of our God and to repair the ruins thereof”. O, dear brethren, we have had to do some repair work. We humbly acknowledge that we have made such repairs necessary, and we need much help to continue in this work, that the house of our God may be free from defilement. In Nehemiah’s day one of the chambers of the house was set aside by the priest to hold the household stuff of Tobijah, one of the enemies of the people of God. Nehemiah cast the stuff out! We need energy to allow nothing that would bring in defilement, that the house of God may be a sphere for the complacent dwelling of God amongst us, a “habitation of God in the Spirit”.

Finally, Ezra says, “And now, what shall we say, our God, after this?”. What shall we say, dear brethren? May we let these things sink deeply into our souls and affect our spirits. Let us lift up our earnest prayer to God that we may truly appreciate the little reviving He has given us; that we may find the Spirit’s gracious help to keep humble; that we may endeavour to go on together walking in the light that shines from the candlestick; that we may increasingly enjoy the presence of God, cleansed from all unrighteousness and acceptable to Him.

I have in mind to speak about being formed according to divine impressions, impressions which we receive maybe privately in reading the Scriptures, or in being together. I note from experience that very often we receive impressions and they come very near to us. We think about them, but the many things we are occupied with very easily take them away from us.

So I think it should be an exercise with us all, young and old, to be more concerned when the Lord is seeking to speak to us that we open our hearts and follow the impressions up with method and diligence so that we may be formed according to His nature.

One of the greatest things we are able to learn in our strangership here is the knowledge of divine Persons. The Lord Jesus, who has come so near to us, has found a way, His own way, into our hearts. He would like us to be more earnestly occupied with His things that His work may develop in us so that we are really ready to be taken up into heaven. I think this word which we have read would help us on these lines. Luke 9: 51 speaks about His “receiving up”, at the time of the mount of transfiguration. You know, the Lord was always ready to be taken into heaven. There was nothing unsuitable, nothing disturbing, with Him. At the start of His service

the voice came, “This is my beloved Son” (Matthew 3: 17), and then again on the mount of transfiguration. Peter would make three tabernacles, but it is important to see that the Father does not allow anyone to intrude upon the uniqueness and preciousness of the Son. So I feel we should be more attached to Him in view of the nearness of His coming to take us to Himself. It says in Revelation, “The Spirit and the bride say, Come” (Revelation 22: 17), and every one who hears it is to say, Come. Do we expect the Lord? The time is near when He will come to take us, then all the children of God will be caught up together to meet Him in the air.

But now it is the time of His rejection and it is a time of formation. I wonder whether we think enough about this time of forming. Mr. Taylor often said that everything which will be displayed in the world to come is formed now in the saints. Should not therefore our exercises be in relation to the coming world and in relation to the One who will be the centre of that world? So it is good to think about that world which we are awaiting, and our desire is to be living more in view of it. It is remarkable to read Mr. Raven’s ministry; almost from the start he shows the importance of our being connected with the world to come. So the question is how far our hearts are really attached to Christ in glory.

There are two persons here, Elijah and Elisha, who seem to have a private history. It is not exactly what is going on publicly. What is outside we find more in the first chapter, where there is decline. So if we look around we feel really sorry about the scattering of God’s people and the iniquity, which is increasing. But God is surely securing something for His own heart and for His own pleasure. So I wondered whether these places where
Elisha went with Elijah would help us to be more suitable, to be in a state of expecting the near coming of our Lord. They both went together and Elijah in a sense tests Elisha in saying,

“Abide here, I pray thee; for Jehovah has sent me to Bethel”. You wonder when you read it what it really meant. We remember that Mr. Raven speaks about the course of the testimony and the tests connected with it. He said he would not persuade anybody to go in this way of separation because of the tests connected with it. On the other hand, I think it is really the love which attaches you to Christ which makes you feel you cannot be without Him. You really feel you cannot be without the Lord Jesus. That is so for the young ones and for every one of us, that we cannot be without Him and we would not be apart from His movements.
We would be in accord with the way in which He moves.

So Elijah goes on his way. He says several times, “Abide here, I pray thee”. I think that is only to bring out the genuineness of the work of God in every one of us. You think about the Lord Himself, how He could meet in real humanity, in flesh and blood conditions as ourselves, sin apart, and in holy dependence, every enemy, and bring to pass God’s will under the uttermost of trying circumstances. So you look at Him who has died for your sins.
You appreciate Him as the only One who was able to die for your sins, who cleared them away for ever from before the face of God. And He went through here in full dependence—
showing in every footstep and in every act, in everything He did, perfect dependence as Man.

Is that not something for every one of our hearts to think about?—what God had in that Man here, and how His pleasure was secured in Him, how something was secured in Christ here which is for His heart for all eternity. Think about what results through the greatness of

His death and the reality of His manhood. Well, I would like to try to present His greatness and preciousness so as to affect all our hearts, so that something may be developed by His Spirit which is like Him.

So these two persons could not be separated. “As Jehovah liveth, and as thy soul liveth, I will not leave thee!”. Is that not a good start, and not only a good start but a fresh appeal to our hearts to say, “I will not leave thee!”? The Lord Jesus desires to attach you to Himself, and how He values you, in the world where He is rejected. So they start at Gilgal. We remember the fact that it was at Gilgal, after they went through Jordan, that they experienced circumcision. I think there was really life working in their souls and in their lives which attracted them to the ark, and brought them through the Jordan, and there they could find that the flesh had no place in the thoughts of God. I think that really it is a lesson we have to learn all our lives through, how the flesh works in different settings. Think about the exercises in our young lives as to Amalek. It says in Exodus 17: 16 that “Jehovah will have war against Amalek from generation to generation”. But here we really find power working and see how Elisha is attracted to Elijah because of his affection for him, and what he appreciated in Elijah; he would not give up and leave him—“As Jehovah liveth, and as thy soul liveth, I will not leave thee! So they went down to Bethel”.

I think if we choose to find our place with Christ crucified, then we value this aspect of His death, His being crucified and being cut off. This would just make way for being able to be together with Him in God’s house, of which Bethel speaks, in a place where God pleases to reveal Himself.
self. We think about the Lord Himself and it is said, “The zeal of thy house devours me”

(John 2: 17), when He dealt with what was going on wrongly in the temple. So we find persons who are able to judge what they are in the flesh and therefore can appreciate that God likes to reveal Himself. He is revealing Himself where He has put His name, and then also, as we know, the Lord said, “Where two or three are gathered together unto my name, there am I in the midst”, Matthew 18: 20. That does not mean that we have exactly a claim to it, but we just like to provide conditions where He is able to speak to us, and where He is able to make known to us the preciousness of His Person. So what an experience it is to be on this line of God’s thoughts, and not to be diverted through all kinds of thoughts of men. God has established His testimony in relation to His thoughts, and I think every one of us should really appreciate the good teaching, how the Lord Himself was pleased to come in in the time of Mr. Darby and has helped His people so distinctly until now. But the exercise should be still with us to maintain a place that the Lord is pleased with, not letting one thought which He has recovered in His goodness fall to the ground.

In the letter to Philadelphia the Lord says, “Hold fast what thou hast, that no one take thy crown”, Revelation.3: 11. I wonder, dear brethren, if we think about that. Is not the Lord attaching a great value to this at the present moment? We think about the times of the martyrs and all they went through. They gave up their lives, and how the Lord valued that, but I wonder whether we all think, or can imagine, how the Lord appreciates every one who seeks to keep what He has secured in this time of recovery, including that choice thought that He has in His heart, Christ and the assembly.

It is a mystery which came out, in times of great trial, in Paul’s writings. How we should really humble ourselves but, on the other hand, let us cling to these precious thoughts and desire to work them out in our local places, as one said, dying for the truth. I suppose every one here has gone through much exercise as to the solemn happenings in 1970 and 1972, .and it is remarkable, if you think back, how very early decline came in after the apostle Paul’s departure. We can only say that that was due to failure in responsibility. But how sure we can be that everything is secured in this Man and He will bring through something (we can say this without being presumptuous) for His own heart. So we really love, young and old, to give Him the first place in all our hearts.

Elijah and Elisha came to Jericho and it says, “And the sons of the prophets that were at Jericho drew near to Elisha and said to him, Dost thou know that Jehovah will take away thy master from over thy head today?”. There were these thoughts in their hearts of knowing quite a bit of the truth, but at the end we find from these men that they had no part really in the receiving up of Elijah. They told Elisha to send and look for him. They said they knew these things, and it really tests one’s own heart as to how far we are really in accord with the reality of what we know. I thought if we could follow this exercise, something would develop for the pleasure of God. It says that as they came to Jericho Elijah said, “Abide here, I pray thee; for Jehovah has sent me to the Jordan”. Jericho, as we know, was built up again, also there was a curse on it. The curse is on the whole course of this world. Dear brethren, we have to go through it, but in our hearts we would be attracted to greater things which are of much more importance and value. Everything that is attached

to this place where the curse is is spoken about in Revelation 18 where it says, “Great Babylon has fallen, has fallen”. All this is to bear very closely on my own heart, and on all our hearts, but the motive behind facing these exercises is love for the Lord Jesus, love for this glorious Man in heaven who likes to attract us to Himself. So we are able to go around this city, Jericho, as Israel did. We are unable to bring it down, only God is able for that; God is able to come in with His own power. But let us remember that He gives power to sustain us right through these exercises in attachment to our Lord.

Then they go to the Jordan, the place where we find we have died with Christ. Every one of us would surely have the desire to be in the good of that. We appreciate His death, but the question is whether, in time of testing, we are able to be in accord with the Jordan. We know of these exercises, may every one be going through them; God likes to give us power to be in the gain of them. So Elijah took his mantle and wrapped it together and smote the waters and the Jordan was divided. So the power of death has been broken, the Lord has gone through.

What a glorious Victor we have, beloved brethren. And in this sense, going through these exercises one by one, I wondered if something would develop in us which might be more for the glory of God and for His testimony for as long as we are here, for His name’s sake.

I was impressed with these scriptures when our brother was speaking about lifting up our eyes. In Exodus 24 we find persons who were qualified to go up, to see things that we do not see with our natural eyes. What a moment it must have been for these persons to see the God of Israel. And this God is our God. We can say it through grace and through mercy, the God who makes Himself to be seen. How wonderful that He has made Himself manifest, so that we can see His glory and majesty in the face of Jesus. What a God we have! And if we ponder over His ways with His people it has ever been the desire of God to make Himself wondrously known to His people. And not only that, but He desired a dwelling place among them.

What specially impressed me is what is said in Exodus 24: 10, “And there was under his feet as it were work of transparent sapphire, and as it were the form of heaven for clearness”. I think that transparency and clearness are what divine Persons desire in this time, to form these features in the saints. What pleasure God must have in those who are prepared to be formed according to His own thoughts, suggested here in what was under His feet. We find this feature of transparency again in Revelation 21: 21, “… and the street of the city pure gold, as transparent glass”. There are other references in that section to transparency, suggesting

that the Lord desires that in this time of formation this feature of transparency may come more into evidence. It is brought about by pressure, and by exercise, and in character is like the pearl mentioned in the same verse. I was thinking that we should be encouraged, that we should, as our brother said, renew our strength and mount up and see the God who has made Himself known. Thus may we continue in the pathway of His testimony, for His honour.

As regards Revelation 21, this city was seen coming down; as we have often said, it is the masterpiece of God. I was thinking that as we, by the power of the Holy Spirit, appropriate this place of nearness to God we shall look out more and more for this wonderful moment,

“The holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down out of the heaven from God, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband”. What a moment, beloved brethren! What freshness and what beauty the Lord will see in the vessel He has secured for Himself at such immense cost, for His honour and for His glory. It is something that will never get old, something that will satisfy eternally the heart of God, and our hearts. We should be persons who are satisfied and happy and bright, in view of these wonderful things.

So let us be encouraged through what we are finding. Let us be more concerned as to these holy matters, so that the praise of God is more and more enriched. What cause we have to prostrate ourselves before Him who has brought about all these things and who will bring us soon to the actuality of them. Let us thus be encouraged, and let us go on and see that we keep more in nearness to Him, for His name’s sake.

articles.title: “THE TIME OF MY RELEASE IS COME”
articles.author: D. T. Howie
articles.meeting: Word at the burial of Mrs, B. Falconer

paragraphs.text: A simple thought, beloved brethren, as to what Paul says in this epistle to one to whom he could speak as his beloved child. Paul here is about to leave this scene, no doubt dying the death of a martyr; a time of great pressure was upon him. And how often pressure does come upon us in many ways; the pressure of circumstances, the pressure perhaps of ill-health, and then the pressure that death brings in. But in all these circumstances we not only prove by faith the help and support and encouragement of the Lord, but what happens is that affections are drawn out amongst us.

This is a time when there is grief and mourning, but then it is also a time when love comes into expression in a way that perhaps it has not before, but the great thought is that it should remain, because love working among us in this way has a great binding effect upon the saints.

So the death of our beloved sister is to bear its own fruit. She bore fruit in her own pathway, as seen in the way in which she worked out her life as a simple christian—and what a pattern she has been for those who looked upon her.
Here Paul says, “For I am already being poured out, and the time of my release is come. I have combated the good combat, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith”. What a challenge that is

for those of us remaining! We may have started the race, and we may so far have kept the faith, but are we going to finish? And are we going to finish as Paul finished? He finished in a spirit of triumph and victory and in the spirit of our Lord Jesus Christ, considering for those who remained. This was how he considered for Timothy. He appeals to him and says, “Use diligence to come to me quickly”. I believe, beloved brethren, that where Paul’s truth is held it affords a sphere of salvation for us. I believe Timothy would realise that. You might say,

‘Paul, you need Timothy’s presence’. Well, I think Timothy needed Paul’s presence. I think safety for us all at the present time is to be where the truth that Paul has given is held in its fulness. So he says, “Use diligence to come to me quickly”. Let us give that prayerful consideration as before the Lord. We are to be keepers and maintainers of the truth. If we are not in it, the Lord would bring us to it. So Paul makes this appeal, ‘Come and share these conditions’. Winter conditions were coming; there is suffering where Paul is, but he says,
“Use diligence to come to me quickly”.

Then Paul says, “Salute Prisca and Aquila”. He knows there are those who will continue; he has this company at the end. There is no word here as to the death that he is to face, only the thought that he is going out in triumph; no word of the pressure of the sufferings that he is having to endure, but the thought of what he is going to; what he has enjoyed, and what he will enjoy. “Salute Prisca and Aquila, and the house of Onesiphorus. Erastus remained in Corinth, but Trophimus I left behind in Miletus sick”; that is, things are to be worked out locally, and worked out in affection. “Use diligence to come before winter”—the place of warmth is where Paul’s ministry

has been held and practised in faithfulness before God. Paul adds, “Eubulus salutes thee, and Pudens … and the brethren all”. Paul is not alone at the end. There was a time when he was alone (2 Timothy 4: 16) and at that time he knew the presence and comfort of the Lord.

Beloved brethren, there is One who will never leave us. This is not a position of weakness; there are these brethren and households. Things are being worked out in affection; that is, Paul’s sufferings are having a result in a practical and living way. So he says, “The Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit”, and the footnote says that is singular; then Paul adds,

“Grace be with you”, that is a collective thought. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ is available to us, to maintain us all to the very end. May we know what it is to be in the pathway of faith and finish as Paul finished, and as our dear sister finished, in the triumph and might of the work of Christ.

articles.title: THE SPIRIT OF LIFE
articles.author: D. Wright
articles.meeting: Substance of word in meeting for ministry

paragraphs.text: I would like to say a brief word as to the Spirit of life. We have often been reminded, especially from John’s writings, that the only answer to the growing state of apostasy all around us is life. This life can only characterise us as having its source in the Spirit of life.
One feels for oneself that in our gatherings together not only

should right things be said, but what is said should be in the power of the Spirit of life. The Spirit would always draw attention to the Man who fills God’s presence, would draw us to where the Lord Jesus is, as we sang in our opening hymn, ‘Thy radiancy draws us apart’. The Spirit would occupy us with His glories.

In John 4: 14 the Lord Jesus says, “The water which I shall give him shall become in him a fountain of water, springing up into eternal life”. “Shall become” seems to indicate a certain process. The more I make way for the Spirit in myself the more there will be this springing up. Then in John 7: 38 the Lord says, “Out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water”. It raises a challenge as to whether we can be a channel through which the Spirit can make known His present mind.

In the epistle to the Romans we have the line of the flesh, which brings in death, and the line of the Spirit, which brings in life. There could not be a greater contrast; the two are totally opposed. So Romans 8: 2 says, “The law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus has set me free from the law of sin and of death”. It has set me free to serve God. In verse 6 we have the great contrast again, “The mind of the flesh is death; but the mind of the Spirit life and peace”. It is not only that one line of things is to be negated, but that the line of life springing up by the Spirit is to be in evidence.

When we come to verse 11 we have a very wonderful line of truth, that is, that the Spirit of Him that has raised up Jesus from among the dead dwells in us. Think of the power that was involved in raising Jesus from among the dead! We are told in chapter 6 that “Christ has been raised up from among the dead by the glory of the Father”, and the Spirit

of that One dwells in us. We may get used to hearing these great truths spoken of; let us stop and ponder for a moment the greatness of it, that a divine Person indwells us. The Spirit is in us, therefore He is able to quicken us. Do you have the experience in an occasion like this, or a reading meeting, of a brother saying something that quickens you, that brings about a certain springing up in you Godward? Beloved brethren, if we have this experience, it is evidence that the Spirit of life is operating amongst us. I am sure we do experience it, but I would desire to experience it more. I say again, I feel the importance of not only right things being said, but that they are said in the power of the Spirit of life; this would bring in quickening, and a greater yield for the heart of our blessed God. Satan has no answer when this life is in evidence, because it is a life which has its source in the Spirit, and cannot be imitated.

Our portion will ever be in light, which characterises the presence of God who is light and in whom is no darkness at all (1 John 1: 5). The Lord Jesus was light in a dark world and it is by the Spirit that light is maintained here now. Light has ever marked the operations of God who brought it in creatorially and then amongst His people. When Egypt was in darkness, the Israelites had “light in their dwellings” (Exodus 10: 23). There
was light continually linked with the tabernacle, both from the lamps within and from the fire without by night.

We have been brought into the light as it shone in Jesus. Our fellowship is in it. We are responsible to walk in the light, and any element of darkness with ourselves can be met because “the blood of Jesus Christ His Son cleanses us from all sin”, 1 John 1: 7. In the heavenly city there is no night—the portion of the redeemed is ever in light, both now and eternally. We have been delivered from the authority of darkness and brought into Christ’s blessed kingdom (Colossians 1: 12, 13) of which He is the glorious Sun.
Kingston, Ont.
Lord, I would have Thy presence all the way,
Both day and night;
Not only in the sunshine of the day
When all seems bright,
But when the evening shadows gather round
And fear assails,
When danger lurks ahead and foes abound
When courage fails
And faith is well-nigh lost. Lord from above
Hold Thou my hand!
I need the strength and comfort of Thy love,
Thy blest command,
To bring my restless will beneath Thy sway,
That I may rest
And know the journey ends in perfect day.
Most truly blest
Are they who prove Thy love and wait for Thee
Until the night
Has passed with all its fear and mystery;
Then glorious light
Will break, as when of old Thy voice was heard
Upon the sea,
And stormy wind and wave obeyed Thy word
So instantly.
Till then be Thou my Guide, my Strength, my Stay!
I lean on Thee
And trust Thy faithful love, although Thy way
Be in the sea.

“I HAVE THOUGHT ON MY WAYS” (Psalm 119: 59) It is important to take stock of our ways. Perhaps some “grievous way” (Psalm 139: 24) is creeping in. Perhaps there are habits or tastes which are hindering spiritual prosperity, interfering with communion. Perhaps reading and prayer are being squeezed out by other things. So let us think on our ways and have grace from the Lord to adjust them where necessary. Then, like the psalmist, we shall not only be able to say, “I have thought on my ways”, but also, “and turned my feet unto thy testimonies”. Later in this psalm (Psalm 119: 168) he can say, “All my ways are before thee”—a safe and happy state!

“THY HANDS HAVE MADE ME AND FASHIONED ME” (Psalm 119: 73) It is a most affecting thought to the believer that we have each been the subject of divine care and formation. This relates to our bodies and also to spiritual formation. We have been made for divine pleasure. But the thought of

fashioning seems to go further, involving beauty and adornment. Experience with God in the christian’s life, teaching, and ministry are all intended to bring about the fashioning of the work of God, so that we come out, not in conformity to the world, not in the characteristics of the flesh, but increasingly in the features of the life of Christ. So in Luke 7: 44 the Lord says,
“Seest thou this woman?”. Everyone there knew what she had been, but now the Lord was calling attention, with holy delight, to what she now was, the product of His own skilful fashioning.

I want the morning star in my heart (the hope of Christ before the day, coming to receive the church to Himself—for the morning star is given to them that overcome) to cheer my soul through the long and dreary night, which is yet darker now than it was then, but still far spent, as the darkness of the night always thickens till again the dawn of another day rise beyond on the other side of heaven and the morning star appear to fix the eye of the watchful and waiting soul, and cheer the heart with a sure and certain hope. And what, then, do we want of the things of this dark place, which is now under judgment for having nailed God’s Son on the cross? Do not you, therefore, be seeking the riches, the honours, the power of this world, on which Christ is coming to execute judgment. One ray of the glory of Christ will at once wither up all the glory of this defiled world like an autumn leaf. Do not you, therefore, go on mixing yourself up with the world and heaping up riches. What will you do with them

when Christ comes? Remember the Lord is at hand. But do I keep separate from this world merely because it is going to be judged? Certainly not. My whole portion for time and eternity is in Christ; the day-star has arisen in my heart. I am separated from the world by affection and not by fear.
paragraphs.source: J. N. Darby (‘Coll. Wrtgs.’(N.S.) Vol. 5, p.319)

paragraphs.text: We might refer to Exodus 31: 13–17. You do not get earlier what is stated there. God is bringing it in there for the purpose of impressing us with the necessity of taking time for divine things not for service, but for contemplation. What we need is that in the power of the Spirit we should absorb what revelation affords for us. That passage is the finish of the instruction on the mountain, and shows what God had in mind in view of His house; that His people should be restful spiritually and take time to contemplate divine things.

God has pleasure in anyone coming forward to accept responsibility. If there is something to be done, and someone comes forward and says, ‘I will do it’, that pleases the Lord. Thus it may come down to any single one of us, in taking up responsibility, to see that things are carried out.
